name: ANSI NOR gate drawn as negative-input AND
summary: AND outline with bubbled inputs, the De Morgan form of a NOR that reads as all inputs low gives a high output.
description: A NOR gate is equivalent to an AND gate with inverted inputs. Drawing the AND outline with input bubbles states the design intent directly: the output is high only when all inputs are low. It is the same device as a NOR gate with the outline chosen to match the signal sense.

This representation is common for all-clear logic where each input is an active-high fault, so all-low means healthy. It also helps when reviewing permissive chains, because the outline reads as a conjunction of conditions.
As with any De Morgan form, the part fitted is still a NOR device. The parts list, pin numbering and gate section remain those of the NOR package.
readingNotes: Read bubbled inputs on an AND outline as a NOR device.
Confirm the part reference matches a NOR package.
drawingChecklist: Use the form consistently for active-low or all-clear logic.
Document the De Morgan convention in the legend.
distinction: An AND outline with only an output bubble is a NAND; here the bubbles are on the inputs.
